recommendation_summary: Right now, replace the row fetch and in-memory object count with a PostgreSQL SELECT count(*) on the unpaid condition. A partial index is added only if EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows the query is still slow. Kafka, CQRS and Redis are rejected because a projection updates after commit and can't guarantee request-time committed counts. No new services or topics are proposed, and no requirement is left unmet.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You need the unpaid-invoice count under one second and reflecting committed invoices at request time; Kafka, CQRS, and Redis come from peer trends and an approved budget, not from a failure that needs them.
labels.Deleted: Kafka topics, CQRS projection, Redis cache.
labels.Bottleneck: The endpoint loads every unpaid invoice row and builds objects in application memory just to count them.
labels.Checked myself: Nothing observed directly; from your description, the endpoint returns only the count, has no other reader, and users report it slow.

note: All four record lines come before a bounded in-database aggregate that keeps request-time semantics, and the reply makes no claim of having observed anything itself.
